title.value: Manage many Copilot agent chats across workspaces

introduction.value: A poster describes organizing many GitHub Copilot agent chats across multiple workspaces and projects in their daily workflow.

method.value: The poster set up a file-based multi-agent workflow in VS Code using workspaces, folders, and GitHub prompt files rather than scripts or frameworks. An orchestrator workspace held assignments, per-agent communication files, and a history folder; prompt commands like /assign Python "task 1" found an available agent, pulled the matching task from a spec, summarized it into that agent’s assignment file, and the human then opened the relevant agent workspace with access to the needed repo or repo folder.

outcome.value: It helped them manage work across about 100 repos by replacing many separate Copilot chats with a handful of reusable agents that could carry context forward. They had only used it for about a week, though, so longer-run context bloat and other pain points were still untested.

notes.value: The main catch was scope: it was built to tame roughly 100 repos and 100 Copilot chat contexts, but the poster said it was still new and they planned to archive communication into history weekly.

source_text.body:
Manage many Copilot agent chats across workspaces
A poster describes organizing many GitHub Copilot agent chats across multiple workspaces and projects in their daily workflow.
Done with
GH
GitHub Copilot
What they did
The poster set up a file-based multi-agent workflow in VS Code using workspaces, folders, and GitHub prompt files rather than scripts or frameworks. An orchestrator workspace held assignments, per-agent communication files, and a history folder; prompt commands like /assign Python "task 1" found an available agent, pulled the matching task from a spec, summarized it into that agent’s assignment file, and the human then opened the relevant agent workspace with access to the needed repo or repo folder.
How it went
It helped them manage work across about 100 repos by replacing many separate Copilot chats with a handful of reusable agents that could carry context forward. They had only used it for about a week, though, so longer-run context bloat and other pain points were still untested.
Worth knowing
The main catch was scope: it was built to tame roughly 100 repos and 100 Copilot chat contexts, but the poster said it was still new and they planned to archive communication into history weekly.
Try it yourself
with
GitHub Copilot
Copy prompt
I have several Copilot agent chats across these workspaces: [list workspaces or projects]. Help me set up a simple system for organizing them, such as naming conventions for chats, a notes file per project with current status and next steps, and a way to resume a chat after a break. Give me a template I can copy into each project.
Original source: https://www.reddit.com/r/GithubCopilot/comments/1r6vcbi/orchestration_and_agents
